title: OIDC Authorization Code (Confidential Client)
subtitle: The server-side web-app flow. Step through it and see why the tokens never touch the browser — and how to read the front channel in the Network tab.

steps.label: User visits a protected page
steps.lede: The user hits a page that needs a session. The app has no session yet, so it builds an authorization request and stores state + nonce. Nothing secret has left the server.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network tab, enable Preserve log so the redirects aren’t cleared, and set the filter to Doc — the hops in this flow are full-page document navigations.

steps.label: Redirect to /authorize
steps.lede: The app 302-redirects the browser to the authorization endpoint. This front channel carries no secret — just the public client_id, the redirect_uri, the requested scopes, and the CSRF/replay guards.
steps.devtools: Find the request to /authorize and read the Query String Parameters. Confirm response_type=code and that no client_secret is present — the secret stays on the server. Copy state; you’ll match it on the way back.

steps.label: Login + consent screen
steps.lede: The IdP serves its own login page and, if needed, a consent screen for the requested scopes. Credentials are entered against the IdP, never against the app.
steps.devtools: You’ll see the IdP’s own HTML documents and an idp_session cookie set with HttpOnly; Secure (Application tab → Cookies for the IdP origin). Verify the origin is the real IdP before typing a password.

steps.label: Redirect back with code
steps.lede: On success the IdP 302-redirects back to the registered redirect_uri with a short-lived, single-use authorization code and the echoed state.
steps.devtools: Find the 302 whose Location header points at your redirect_uri. The code is in the query string. Verify the returned state equals the one you sent — a mismatch means CSRF; discard the code and do not call /token.

steps.label: Exchange code at /token
steps.lede: The app’s backend posts the code to the token endpoint and authenticates itself with its client secret (here HTTP Basic). This is a server-to-server call — the browser never sees it.
steps.devtools: You will not see this request in the browser — that is the defining property of the confidential-client flow. The Authorization: Basic header decodes to client_id:client_secret (s6BhdRkqt3:cs_synthetic). To inspect it, use backend logs or a proxy (mitmproxy / Charles), never DevTools.

steps.label: Tokens returned
steps.lede: The IdP validates the code, client auth, and redirect_uri, then returns an access token and an ID token (a JWT about the user). These tokens stay on the server side.

jwt.title: Decoded id_token
payload: Issuer — must equal your configured IdP
Stable, opaque user id at this IdP
Must equal the nonce you sent to /authorize
Whether the IdP verified the address

steps.devtools: The id_token never appears in the browser for this flow — decode it from a backend log or proxy capture, not the Network tab. Validation the server must do: verify the signature against the JWKS key named by kid, then check iss, aud == client_id, exp, and that nonce matches the stored value.

steps.label: Establish app session
steps.lede: Having validated the tokens server-side, the app sets its own session cookie and redirects the browser to the logged-in page. The browser holds a cookie, not a token.
steps.devtools: The only thing the browser gains is an app_session cookie (HttpOnly; Secure). Confirm in the Application tab that no access_token or id_token is stored in localStorage / sessionStorage — in a classic confidential-client app there is nothing token-shaped in the browser at all.

steps.label: Signed in
steps.lede: The app renders the dashboard from its server-side session. The authorization code was single-use and is now spent.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire for sign-in. Because the code exchange and the tokens lived only on the back channel, a network eavesdropper on the browser never saw a bearer credential. Replaying the spent code at /token now fails with invalid_grant.
